title: Non-Immune Hydrops, Hypotonia, Encephalopathy, and Liver Failure with Novel Compound Heterozygous <b><i>AHCY</i></b> Mutations
abstract: A late-preterm infant with a prenatal diagnosis of non-immune hydrops was born with hypotonia, poor respiratory effort, chylothorax, encephalopathy, coagulopathy, progressive hepatic failure, and refractory pulmonary hypertension. Life support was withdrawn at 7 days of life due to multisystem organ failure. Rapid whole exome sequencing revealed novel compound heterozygous mutations in the gene encoding S-adenosylhomocysteine hydrolase (<i>AHCY</i>); each novel variant was carried by an asymptomatic parent. Reports of neonates with other <i>AHCY</i> mutations describe a pathology of varying severity. <i>AHCY</i> mutations should be considered when seeking an etiology for neonates with the combination of non-immune hydrops, hypotonia, encephalopathy, and liver failure.
